\subsection{Subgroup calibration diagnostics}
\label{app:subgroup}

The main calibration target throughout this paper is aggregate distributional alignment between
simulated and observed responses; the subgroup analysis below is reported as a diagnostic and is
not a separate validation claim. We compute per-subgroup metrics for the two final protocols
(C7, Direct, $T{=}0.8$ for \texttt{pacdemons}; C11, VS-CoT, $T{=}0.8$ for \texttt{womenwork})
across six substantively important dimensions available in the TGSS metadata: gender, age band,
education, urbanization, ethnic origin, and self-placed political orientation. Subgroup cells
with $n<50$ are suppressed in the tables as substantive estimates but their $n$ is retained for
transparency (0 suppressed cells in
Table~\ref{tab:subgroup-pacdemons}, 0 in Table~\ref{tab:subgroup-womenwork}).

For \texttt{pacdemons}, MCC across reported subgroups spans
[0.167, 0.586] (range 0.420), and minority-class recall spans
[0.278, 0.667]. We emphasize minority recovery rather than overall accuracy
because the positive class (participated in protest) is rare ($\approx$5\% prevalence); subgroup
cells with sparse positive cases are particularly susceptible to recall drops and elevated
false-negative rates, and should not be interpreted as evidence of group-specific failure without
further analysis. For \texttt{womenwork}, Wasserstein-1 across reported subgroups spans
[0.096, 0.308] and the absolute mean error stays within 0.308 Likert
units. We caution against interpreting subgroup Cohen's $\kappa$ as individual-level accuracy:
the main-text $\kappa$ for \texttt{womenwork} is near zero because VS-CoT samples from a
verbalized distribution rather than committing to a single label per respondent; subgroup
$\kappa$ should be read only as a diagnostic of within-group disagreement, not as a per-respondent
prediction-quality estimate.

Taken together, the diagnostic suggests that calibration quality is broadly stable across the
demographic and political subgroups examined, with no dimension producing collapse of the primary
metric. Where deviations are visible, they fall within the multi-seed variance band established
in the main multi-seed stability analysis. We report the full subgroup tables transparently and
treat any large per-cell deviations as limitations rather than as evidence of group-level
miscalibration in either direction.
